contents.html: a. A risk analysis may be defined as an analysis of the threats to and vulnerabilities of a system, expected losses, and selection of countermeasures to reduce the losses to an acceptable level. The requirement for Federal agencies to conduct a risk analysis of an Automated Data Processing (ADP) facility has been in effect since the issuance of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-71, Transmittal Memorandum No. 1 in 1978. The Department of Justice (DOJ) issued Order DOJ 2640.2B and its earlier canceled versions which established the requirement for a risk analysis of DOJ ADP facilities beginning in 1977. The DOJ also issued a detailed risk analysis guidance document for use by DOJ ADP facilities in 1977. A number of Federal agencies, contractors, and university professors have developed risk analysis methodologies, some of which have been automated. Due to the complexity of the risk analysis process, the methodologies generally require considerable time to become knowledgeable of its correct usage and to complete the risk analysis.
contents.html_ja: a. リスク分析は、システムに対する脅威と脆弱性、予想される損失、および損失を許容可能な水準まで減らすための対策の選定を分析するものと定義できます。連邦機関に自動データ処理（ADP）施設のリスク分析の実施を求める要件は、1978 年に行政管理予算局（OMB）Circular A-71, Transmittal Memorandum No. 1 が発行されて以来、有効となっています。司法省（DOJ）は、1977 年からDOJ の ADP 施設にリスク分析を求める Order DOJ 2640.2B と、それ以前の廃止済みの版を発行しました。DOJ は、1977 年に、DOJ の ADP 施設が使用するための詳細なリスク分析ガイダンス文書も発行しました。多くの連邦機関、契約業者および大学教授がリスク分析方法論を開発しており、その一部は自動化されています。リスク分析プロセスは複雑であるため、これらの方法論では一般に、正しい使用方法を習得し、リスク分析を完了するまでにかなりの時間を要します。

contents.html: b. A risk analysis does not enhance security by itself but provides cost effective security recommendations for management consideration. Therefore, there is a need to simplify the risk analysis process to the extent possible, which is the intent of the Simplified Risk Analysis Guidelines (SRAG) contained herein. The SRAG expedites the risk analysis process for the system under evaluation by initially determining if minimum security requirements applicable to the DOJ are met, which eliminates a number of threats and losses from evaluation. Although the SRAG simplifies the risk analysis process, SRAG users should be aware that significant effort by knowledgeable personnel may be required to complete a risk analysis. The SRAG is based on Automated Information System (AIS) security policies, regulations, circulars, and guidelines applicable to the DOJ as well as a review of a number of risk analysis methodologies developed by Government agencies and contractors.
contents.html_ja: b. リスク分析は、それ自体ではセキュリティを高めませんが、管理層が検討するための費用対効果の高いセキュリティ勧告を提供します。したがって、リスク分析のプロセスを可能な限り簡素化する必要があります。これが、ここに収録する簡易リスク分析ガイドライン（SRAG）の意図です。SRAG は、まず DOJ に適用される最小限のセキュリティ要件が満たされているかどうかを判断し、評価対象から多くの脅威と損失を除外することで、評価対象システムのリスク分析プロセスを迅速化します。SRAG はリスク分析プロセスを簡素化しますが、SRAG の利用者は、リスク分析を完了するために、十分な知識と経験を備えた要員による相当な労力が必要になる場合があることに留意すべきです。SRAG は、DOJ に適用される自動情報システム（AIS）のセキュリティ方針、規則、通達およびガイドラインと、政府機関や契約業者が開発した多数のリスク分析方法論のレビューに基づいています。

contents.html: c. After evaluating compliance with the minimum security requirements, additional threats and vulnerabilities not affected by the minimum security requirements are assessed to determine if further analysis is needed. The SRAG or a risk analysis methodology selected by the user can be used for this portion of the risk analysis process. Due to the increasing use of AISs other than mainframes, the SRAG also includes sections on microcomputers/Personal Computers (PCs) and application systems. The sections applicable to mainframes are also applicable to minicomputers and other remotely accessed AISs, including networks of PCs.
contents.html_ja: c. 最小限のセキュリティ要件への準拠を評価した後、最小限のセキュリティ要件の影響を受けない追加の脅威と脆弱性を評価して、さらなる分析が必要かどうかを判断します。リスク分析の工程のこの部分には、SRAG、または利用者が選択したリスク分析方法論を使用できます。メインフレーム以外の AIS の利用が増えていることから、SRAG には、マイクロコンピュータ/パーソナルコンピュータ（PC）とアプリケーションシステムに関する節も含まれています。メインフレームに適用される節は、ミニコンピュータや、PC のネットワークを含む、その他の遠隔からアクセスされる AIS にも適用されます。

contents.html_ja: 2. 背景

contents.html: a. Various risk analysis methodologies have been developed by contractors and agencies since the issuance of the risk analysis guidelines by the National Bureau of Standards (NBS) of Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) Publication (PUB) 31, "Guidelines for ADP Physical Security and Risk Management" in 1974, and FIPS PUB 65, "Guideline for ADP Risk Assessment" in 1979. The NBS publications advocated the use of quantitative techniques assigning dollar values to system losses and estimating the annual probability of threats occurring to cause these losses. Similarly, dollar figures are assigned to the cost of security countermeasures and to the reduction in expected annual losses to determine the cost effectiveness of the security measure.
contents.html_ja: a. 1974 年に米国標準局（NBS）が連邦情報処理標準（FIPS）Publication（PUB）31「Guidelines for ADP Physical Security and Risk Management」を、1979 年に FIPS PUB 65「Guideline for ADP Risk Assessment」を発行してリスク分析のガイドラインを示して以来、契約業者や機関によってさまざまなリスク分析方法論が開発されてきました。NBS の刊行物は、システムの損失に金額を割り当て、それらの損失を引き起こす脅威が発生する年間の確率を見積もる、定量的な技法の使用を提唱していました。同様に、セキュリティ対策の費用と、予想される年間損失の減少分にも金額を割り当て、セキュリティ対策の費用対効果を判断します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.14）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: b. Although the National Institute of Standards and Technology (name of NBS since 1988) has not issued any risk analysis publications recently, they are presently considering methodologies using qualitative analysis in part or as a primary method of risk analysis. The methodologies that have been developed are primarily for the mainframe environment despite the increase in usage of PCs and networks and include the use of both quantitative and qualitative techniques. As stated previously, the SRAG does not require or preclude the use of any specific methodology and may be used to conduct a risk analysis of an AIS in many cases without additional risk analysis guidance.
contents.html_ja: b. 国立標準技術研究所（1988 年以降の NBS の名称）は、最近はリスク分析に関する刊行物を発行していませんが、現在、一部または主要なリスク分析の手法として、定性的分析を用いる方法論を検討しています。これまでに開発された方法論は、PC やネットワークの利用が増えているにもかかわらず、主にメインフレーム環境を対象としており、定量的な技法と定性的な技法の両方の使用を含んでいます。前述のとおり、SRAG は特定の方法論の使用を要求することも、妨げることもなく、多くの場合、追加のリスク分析ガイダンスなしで AIS のリスク分析を実施するために使用できます。

contents.html: a. Accreditation - Accreditation is the official management authorization to operate an AIS or network in a particular security mode with a proscribed set of administrative, environmental, and technical security safeguards in a given operational environment.
contents.html_ja: a. 認定（Accreditation） - 認定とは、所定の運用環境において、管理上、環境上および技術上のセキュリティ保護措置の規定された組み合わせを備えて、特定のセキュリティモードで AIS またはネットワークを運用することに対する、管理層の公式の承認です。

contents.html: b. Automated Information System (AIS) - An AIS is an assembly of computer hardware, software, and/or firmware configured to collect, create, communicate, compute, disseminate, process, store, or control data or information. An AIS will typically consist of ADP system hardware, operating system and application software, associated peripheral devices, and associated data communications equipment. An AIS includes PCs, work stations, and office automation systems.
contents.html_ja: b. 自動情報システム（AIS） - AIS とは、データまたは情報を収集、作成、通信、計算、配布、処理、保管または制御するように構成された、コンピュータのハードウェア、ソフトウェア、またはファームウェア（あるいはそのすべて）の集合体です。AIS は通常、ADP システムのハードウェア、オペレーティングシステムとアプリケーションソフトウェア、関連する周辺装置、および関連するデータ通信装置で構成されます。AIS には、PC、ワークステーションおよびオフィスオートメーションシステムが含まれます。

contents.html: c. Network - A network comprises communications media and all attached components whose responsibility is the transfer of information among a collection of AISs or work stations. Network components include packet switches, front-end computers, network controllers, and technical control devices.
contents.html_ja: c. ネットワーク - ネットワークは、通信媒体と、AIS またはワークステーションの集合の間で情報を転送する責任を負う、接続されたすべての構成要素で構成されます。ネットワークの構成要素には、パケット交換機、フロントエンドコンピュータ、ネットワークコントローラおよび技術制御装置が含まれます。

contents.html: d. Sensitive Application Systems - Systems that process sensitive data or require protection due to the risk and magnitude of loss or harm that could result from improper operation or deliberate manipulation of the application.

contents.html: a. The SRAG approach divides systems requiring risk analyses into three categories: PCs; mainframes, minicomputers, and other remotely accessed AISs; and application systems. Each of these categories is further divided depending on whether nonsensitive, sensitive, or classified information is processed, or whether an application is nonsensitive or sensitive as defined in OMB Circular A-130, Appendix III.
contents.html_ja: a. SRAG の手法は、リスク分析が必要なシステムを 3 つのカテゴリに分けます。PC、メインフレーム・ミニコンピュータ・その他の遠隔からアクセスされる AIS、およびアプリケーションシステムです。これらの各カテゴリは、機微でない情報、機微な情報または機密扱いの情報のどれを処理するか、あるいは、OMB Circular A-130, Appendix III で定義されているように、アプリケーションが機微でないか機微であるかに応じて、さらに分けられます。

contents.html: b. The SRAG includes seven steps that are required to conduct the risk analysis and to document the results. The first two steps are used to provide a description of the AIS, its security concerns, and the security measures in place. In Step 3, the AIS environment is evaluated to determine if minimum security requirements are met. The minimum security requirements are listed for processing nonsensitive, sensitive, and classified information on PCs. It should be noted that the minimum security requirements for processing sensitive information also include the requirements for processing nonsensitive; processing classified information requires meeting the minimum security requirements for classified, sensitive, and nonsensitive information. The minimum security requirements for mainframes, minicomputers, and other remotely accessed AISs are presented in a similar hierarchical structure. Sensitive applications must meet the minimum requirements listed for sensitive and nonsensitive applications.
contents.html_ja: b. SRAG には、リスク分析を実施し、その結果を文書化するために必要な 7 つのステップが含まれています。最初の 2 つのステップは、AIS の記述、そのセキュリティ上の懸念事項、および実施済みのセキュリティ対策を示すために使用します。ステップ 3 では、AIS の環境を評価して、最小限のセキュリティ要件が満たされているかどうかを判断します。最小限のセキュリティ要件は、PC で機微でない情報、機微な情報および機密扱いの情報を処理する場合について列挙されています。機微な情報を処理するための最小限のセキュリティ要件には、機微でない情報を処理するための要件も含まれること、機密扱いの情報の処理には、機密扱い、機微および機微でない情報の最小限のセキュリティ要件を満たすことが必要であることに留意すべきです。メインフレーム、ミニコンピュータ、およびその他の遠隔からアクセスされる AIS の最小限のセキュリティ要件も、同様の階層構造で示されています。機微なアプリケーションは、機微および機微でないアプリケーションについて列挙された最小限の要件を満たさなければなりません。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.16）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: c. The remaining steps are used for the following: To determine from an analysis of threats and losses whether additional security measures need to be considered; to select security measures to comply with the minimum requirements that are not effectively met and to reduce other losses; to provide for cost effective recommendations of security measures; to present the recommendations for a decision by management whether to implement the recommendations or accept the risk; and to document the results. The seven SRAG steps are discussed briefly below, followed by Section 12, which provides instructions for using the SRAG and includes flow charts and other information to assist SRAG users. The last portion of the SRAG is the Appendix, which includes detailed information required to conduct a risk analysis, and a number of tables and work forms for use in conducting and documenting the risk analysis.
contents.html_ja: c. 残りのステップは、次の目的で使用します。脅威と損失の分析から、追加のセキュリティ対策を検討する必要があるかどうかを判断すること、効果的に満たされていない最小限の要件に準拠し、その他の損失を減らすためのセキュリティ対策を選定すること、費用対効果の高いセキュリティ対策の勧告を提示すること、勧告を実施するかリスクを受容するかについて管理層が決定できるよう勧告を提示すること、ならびに結果を文書化することです。SRAG の 7 つのステップを以下に簡潔に説明し、続いて、SRAG の使用手順を示し、フローチャートと、SRAG の利用者を支援するその他の情報を含む第 12 節を置いています。SRAG の最後の部分は付録で、リスク分析の実施に必要な詳細情報と、リスク分析の実施および文書化に使用する多数の表と作業様式が含まれています。

contents.html: a. The purpose of Step 1 is to provide a system description of the AIS including the system hardware, software, and personnel, and a general description of the applications and data processed by the AIS. If a risk analysis of an application system is being conducted, a description of the purpose and use of the system is required. Estimates of the cost of the system components should also be included.
contents.html_ja: a. ステップ 1 の目的は、システムのハードウェア、ソフトウェアおよび要員を含む AIS のシステム記述と、AIS が処理するアプリケーションとデータの一般的な記述を提供することです。アプリケーションシステムのリスク分析を実施する場合は、システムの目的と用途の記述が必要です。システム構成要素の費用の見積りも含めるべきです。

contents.html: b. The detailed information required is listed in Table 1 of the Appendix and includes administrative information such as the name and location of the AIS and the names and phone numbers of AIS security personnel. The purpose of the AIS and the component functions it supports should be noted.
contents.html_ja: b. 必要な詳細情報は付録の表 1 に列挙されており、AIS の名称と所在地、AIS のセキュリティ担当要員の氏名と電話番号などの管理情報を含みます。AIS の目的と、それが支援する構成要素の機能にも留意すべきです。

contents.html: c. The system configuration includes a detailed description of the physical location, system configuration diagram, connections, number of users, system and application personnel, and the application systems. A brief description of the purpose of the applications, their method of data input, and the users of the system data should also be included. Cost information required includes the cost of replacing system hardware and software, and the cost of replacing data. The cost information is useful in determining if security countermeasures to reduce the vulnerabilities and potential losses are cost effective. The information obtained during this step is important in evaluating the potential vulnerabilities of the system and the need for additional security measures. It is only through a review of all system components, the applications processed, and the flow of information that an effective analysis of the potential system vulnerabilities can be obtained.
contents.html_ja: c. システム構成には、物理的な所在地、システム構成図、接続、利用者数、システムおよびアプリケーションの要員、ならびにアプリケーションシステムの詳細な記述が含まれます。アプリケーションの目的、データ入力の方法、システムデータの利用者の簡潔な記述も含めるべきです。必要な費用情報には、システムのハードウェアとソフトウェアの交換費用、およびデータの交換費用が含まれます。費用情報は、脆弱性と潜在的な損失を減らすセキュリティ対策が費用対効果の高いものかどうかを判断するのに役立ちます。このステップで得られる情報は、システムの潜在的な脆弱性と追加のセキュリティ対策の必要性を評価するうえで重要です。システムの潜在的な脆弱性を効果的に分析できるのは、すべてのシステム構成要素、処理されるアプリケーション、および情報の流れをレビューすることによってのみです。

contents.html: 6. STEP 2. AIS SECURITY INFORMATION.
contents.html_ja: 6. ステップ 2. AIS のセキュリティ情報
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.17）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: a. In Step 2 of the risk analysis, security related information for the AIS or application is obtained and documented. The system security measures in effect are identified and documented with a brief evaluation of their effectiveness. Security measures are required even if nonsensitive information is processed to protect the equipment and integrity of the data. However, central to the determination of the need for additional security measures is the type of information processed, whether classified (National Security Information), sensitive (Limited Official Use) or nonsensitive information, and the threats to this information. This information is important in determining which minimum security requirements are applicable. The Appendix contains a list of the factors that should be carefully considered during this step, including a list of security measures (Table 2) and application system data sensitivity and criticality considerations (Table 3 and Work Form 5).
contents.html_ja: a. リスク分析のステップ 2 では、AIS またはアプリケーションに関するセキュリティ関連の情報を入手し、文書化します。実施中のシステムのセキュリティ対策を特定し、その有効性の簡潔な評価とともに文書化します。機微でない情報を処理する場合でも、機器とデータの完全性を保護するために、セキュリティ対策が必要です。しかし、追加のセキュリティ対策の必要性を判断する中心となるのは、処理される情報の種類（機密扱い（国家安全保障情報）、機微（限定公用）、または機微でない情報のいずれか）と、その情報に対する脅威です。この情報は、どの最小限のセキュリティ要件が適用されるかを判断するうえで重要です。付録には、このステップで慎重に検討すべき要因の一覧が収められており、セキュリティ対策の一覧（表 2）と、アプリケーションシステムのデータの機微性と重要度の考慮事項（表 3 および作業様式 5）を含みます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.17）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。
原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。柱・ページ番号（PDF p.18）。

contents.html: b. This step also requires an accurate documentation of the security policies, procedures, and countermeasures currently in effect for the AIS. The security measures in place should include administrative procedures, software and hardware security controls, physical security access controls, personnel security controls, and a security awareness program as listed in Table 2. The current security control environment is important due to its impact on the evaluation of the need for additional security measures.
contents.html_ja: b. このステップでは、AIS に現在実施されているセキュリティ方針、手順および対策の正確な文書化も必要です。実施中のセキュリティ対策には、表 2 に列挙されているとおり、管理手順、ソフトウェアとハードウェアのセキュリティ管理策、物理的なセキュリティのアクセス管理策、要員のセキュリティ管理策、およびセキュリティ意識向上プログラムを含めるべきです。現在のセキュリティ管理策の環境は、追加のセキュリティ対策の必要性の評価に影響を与えるため、重要です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.18）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: c. The person conducting the risk analysis should also obtain information on the impact of data disclosure, modification, destruction, and disruption of processing on the component's ability to meet mission objectives. The information obtained during Step 2 should be documented using Work Forms 2, 3, 4, and 5. Additional information required by this step includes the number and geographical disparity of AIS users, the frequency of use of the system, and the method of accessing the system.
contents.html_ja: c. リスク分析を実施する者は、データの開示、改変、破壊、および処理の中断が、構成要素の任務目標を達成する能力に与える影響に関する情報も入手すべきです。ステップ 2 で得られた情報は、作業様式 2、3、4 および 5 を使用して文書化すべきです。このステップで必要な追加情報には、AIS 利用者の数と地理的な分散、システムの利用頻度、およびシステムへのアクセス方法が含まれます。

contents.html: 7. STEP 3. MINIMUM SECURITY REQUIREMENTS.
contents.html_ja: 7. ステップ 3. 最小限のセキュリティ要件
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.18）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: a. The minimum security requirements for PCs, mainframes, minicomputers, and other remotely accessed AISs, and application systems are listed in Sections 3.1, 3.2, and 3.3 of the Appendix. The requirements of each of these sections are divided into requirements for nonsensitive, sensitive, and classified processing for Sections 3.1 and 3.2, and nonsensitive and sensitive applications for Section 3.3. The minimum security requirements are hierarchical in structure, so that requirements for processing lower sensitivity levels also are applicable to all higher sensitivity levels.
contents.html_ja: a. PC、メインフレーム、ミニコンピュータ、その他の遠隔からアクセスされる AIS、およびアプリケーションシステムの最小限のセキュリティ要件は、付録の第 3.1 節、第 3.2 節および第 3.3 節に列挙されています。これらの各節の要件は、第 3.1 節と第 3.2 節では機微でない処理、機微な処理および機密扱いの処理に、第 3.3 節では機微でないアプリケーションと機微なアプリケーションに分けられています。最小限のセキュリティ要件は階層構造になっており、より低い機微性レベルの処理の要件は、より高いすべての機微性レベルにも適用されます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.18）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: b. This step requires a review of the minimum security requirements as listed in the Appendix for the AIS or application under evaluation. The review also requires an evaluation of the effectiveness of the in-place security measures in meeting the security requirement. The person conducting the risk analysis must identify all security measures implemented to comply with the minimum security requirements, assess their effectiveness in meeting the requirement, and document the results. Any of the minimum requirements that are not met will be addressed in Step 5 where the selection of additional countermeasures will be considered.
contents.html_ja: b. このステップでは、評価対象の AIS またはアプリケーションについて、付録に列挙された最小限のセキュリティ要件をレビューする必要があります。このレビューでは、実施中のセキュリティ対策がセキュリティ要件を満たすうえでどの程度有効かの評価も必要です。リスク分析を実施する者は、最小限のセキュリティ要件に準拠するために実施されているすべてのセキュリティ対策を特定し、要件を満たすうえでの有効性を評価し、結果を文書化しなければなりません。満たされていない最小限の要件は、追加の対策の選定を検討するステップ 5 で扱います。

contents.html: 8. STEP 4. ANALYSIS OF THREATS AND LOSSES.
contents.html_ja: 8. ステップ 4. 脅威と損失の分析
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.19）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: a. The purpose of Step 4 is to evaluate threats and losses to determine if consideration of additional security measures to reduce the losses is required. Additional threats and vulnerabilities and resultant losses that were not fully addressed by the minimum security requirements are considered during this step. Typical threats and losses for each sensitivity level are presented in Section 4 of the Appendix; additional threats and losses not listed in Section 4 but applicable to the system should also be considered.
contents.html_ja: a. ステップ 4 の目的は、脅威と損失を評価して、損失を減らす追加のセキュリティ対策を検討する必要があるかどうかを判断することです。最小限のセキュリティ要件では十分に扱われなかった追加の脅威、脆弱性およびその結果としての損失は、このステップで検討します。各機微性レベルの典型的な脅威と損失は付録の第 4 節に示されています。第 4 節に列挙されていませんが、システムに該当する追加の脅威と損失も検討すべきです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.19）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: b. The likelihood of a threat and the potential loss that could be caused by the threat are considered and estimated on a qualitative basis (very low, low, moderate, high, very high). If the threat probability is estimated as less than moderate (low, very low) and the loss is not estimated as very high, the risk is not considered significant and security measures are not considered for the threat-loss pair. If the risk is deemed significant, security measures to comply with the requirement are selected during Step 5. The applicable threats and losses, the estimate of their probability or impact, and the determination if the risk is significant are documented to complete this step.
contents.html_ja: b. 脅威の可能性と、その脅威によって生じうる潜在的な損失は、定性的に（非常に低い、低い、中程度、高い、非常に高い）検討し、見積もります。脅威の確率が中程度未満（低い、非常に低い）と見積もられ、かつ損失が非常に高いとは見積もられない場合、そのリスクは重大とはみなされず、その脅威と損失の組み合わせについてセキュリティ対策は検討されません。リスクが重大とみなされた場合、要件に準拠するためのセキュリティ対策は、ステップ 5 で選定されます。該当する脅威と損失、それらの確率または影響の見積り、およびリスクが重大かどうかの判断を文書化して、このステップを完了します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.19）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: 9. STEP 5. SELECTION OF SECURITY MEASURES.
contents.html_ja: 9. ステップ 5. セキュリティ対策の選定
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.19）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: a. Security measures are selected during Step 5 based upon the results of tasks previously completed in Steps 3 and 4. The selection includes security measures to comply with the minimum security requirements that are not met (Step 3) and to reduce the threats/losses where the risk is significant (Step 4).
contents.html_ja: a. セキュリティ対策は、ステップ 3 と 4 で完了した作業の結果に基づいて、ステップ 5 で選定します。この選定には、満たされていない最小限のセキュリティ要件に準拠するためのセキュリティ対策（ステップ 3）と、リスクが重大な脅威・損失を減らすためのセキュリティ対策（ステップ 4）が含まれます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.19）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: b. Suggested security measures are listed in the Appendix but SRAG users may consider other security measures applicable to their operational environment. The security measures selected and the relevant requirements of Steps 3 and 4 should be documented. The security measures selected to comply with the minimum security requirements of Step 3 are used as recommendations in Step 7; the security measures selected to reduce expected losses of significant threats/losses of Step 4 will go through the cost benefit analysis process of Step 6.
contents.html_ja: b. 推奨されるセキュリティ対策は付録に列挙されていますが、SRAG の利用者は、自らの運用環境に適用できる他のセキュリティ対策を検討してもよいです。選定したセキュリティ対策と、ステップ 3 および 4 の関連する要件は、文書化すべきです。ステップ 3 の最小限のセキュリティ要件に準拠するために選定されたセキュリティ対策は、ステップ 7 で勧告として使用されます。ステップ 4 の重大な脅威・損失について予想される損失を減らすために選定されたセキュリティ対策は、ステップ 6 の費用便益分析の工程を経ます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.19）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: 10. STEP 6. COST BENEFIT ANALYSIS.
contents.html_ja: 10. ステップ 6. 費用便益分析
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.20）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: a. A cost benefit analysis of the security measures selected to respond to the threat/loss analysis of Step 4 is conducted during this step to consider their cost effectiveness and to provide the rationale and justification for recommending security measures to management for action. The security measures that are not considered cost effective based on the cost benefit analysis are dropped from further consideration. A cost benefit analysis is not conducted for security measures selected to meet minimum security requirements but cost information on these measures should be provided for the management decision process of Step 7. Work Form 9 can be used to provide security measure cost information or information on benefits of the required security measure.
contents.html_ja: a. ステップ 4 の脅威・損失の分析に対応するために選定されたセキュリティ対策の費用便益分析は、このステップで実施され、費用対効果を検討し、管理層が措置を講じるためにセキュリティ対策を勧告する根拠と正当性を示します。費用便益分析に基づいて費用対効果が高くないとみなされたセキュリティ対策は、以後の検討から外されます。最小限のセキュリティ要件を満たすために選定されたセキュリティ対策については費用便益分析を実施しませんが、これらの対策の費用情報は、ステップ 7 の管理層の意思決定の工程に提供すべきです。作業様式 9 は、セキュリティ対策の費用情報、または必要なセキュリティ対策の便益に関する情報を提供するために使用できます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.20）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: b. The costs can be expressed in terms of dollars based on the cost of security hardware or software, personnel resources, or impact on the AIS operation. The expression of costs and benefits in annualized dollar terms where practical is recommended to provide management with a sound basis for a decision on implementation of security safeguards. Alternatively, the costs can be expressed in qualitative terms.
contents.html_ja: b. 費用は、セキュリティのハードウェアまたはソフトウェアの費用、要員の資源、または AIS の運用への影響に基づいて、金額で表すことができます。セキュリティ保護措置の実施に関する決定に確かな根拠を管理層に提供するために、実際的な場合には、費用と便益を年換算の金額で表すことが推奨されます。あるいは、費用を定性的な言葉で表すこともできます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.20）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: c. The benefits consist of reduction in the threat occurrence and/or loss impact and include any beneficial impact on mission operations due to increased protection of DOJ information against unauthorized disclosure, modification, and destruction, or disruption of information processing. The benefits should be identified and estimated in quantitative or qualitative terms. Similar to the cost estimates, expression of the benefits in quantitative terms of reduced annualized losses is recommended where practical. The alternative is to estimate the benefits in qualitative terms.
contents.html_ja: c. 便益は、脅威の発生の減少、または損失の影響の減少（あるいはその両方）で構成され、DOJ の情報を、無許可の開示、改変、破壊、または情報処理の中断から保護する度合いが高まることによる、任務運営への有益な影響を含みます。便益は、定量的または定性的な言葉で特定し、見積もるべきです。費用の見積りと同様に、実際的な場合には、年換算の損失の減少という定量的な言葉で便益を表すことが推奨されます。代替の方法は、便益を定性的な言葉で見積もることです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.20）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: d. The person conducting the risk analysis must decide which of the security measures are justified based on the cost benefit analysis and forward these as recommendations for management consideration in Step 7. The results of the cost benefit analysis including the identification and estimate of costs and benefits for each security measure and the evaluation of its cost effectiveness should be documented using Work Form 9 of the Appendix.
contents.html_ja: d. リスク分析を実施する者は、費用便益分析に基づいてどのセキュリティ対策が正当化されるかを決定し、それらをステップ 7 で管理層が検討するための勧告として提出しなければなりません。各セキュリティ対策の費用と便益の特定と見積り、および費用対効果の評価を含む費用便益分析の結果は、付録の作業様式 9 を使用して文書化すべきです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.20）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: 11. STEP 7. RECOMMENDATIONS FOR MANAGEMENT DECISION.
contents.html_ja: 11. ステップ 7. 管理層の意思決定のための勧告
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.21）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: a. The final step is to present the cost effective security recommendations to higher level management for a decision on whether to implement individual recommendations. A proposed schedule for implementing security measures should be provided where appropriate. Management must decide whether to provide the funding or personnel resources, or accept the operational impact that may be required for some security recommendations.
contents.html_ja: a. 最後のステップは、個々の勧告を実施するかどうかを決定してもらうために、費用対効果の高いセキュリティの勧告を上位の管理層に提示することです。適切な場合には、セキュリティ対策を実施するための提案スケジュールを提供すべきです。管理層は、資金や要員の資源を提供するか、一部のセキュリティの勧告に必要となりうる運用上の影響を受け入れるかを決定しなければなりません。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（PDF p.21）と OCR の文字を語ごとに照合。

contents.html: b. The alternative is for management to accept the risk to the security of DOJ information. contents.html: f. A flow chart of the SRAG process is contained in Figure 1 (Page 12). The risk analysis proceeds through consecutive steps from Step 1 through Step 7. The first two steps involve gathering information on the system including relevant security information. The third step consists of determining if the security measures in place effectively meet the applicable minimum security requirements. If a minimum security requirement is not met, security measures to meet the requirement are selected in Step 5 and are included in the recommendations provided to management in Step 7 for approval or disapproval.
contents.html_ja: f. SRAG の工程のフローチャートは、図 1（12 ページ）に収められています。リスク分析は、ステップ 1 からステップ 7 まで順に進みます。最初の 2 つのステップでは、関連するセキュリティ情報を含む、システムに関する情報を収集します。3 番目のステップは、実施中のセキュリティ対策が、該当する最小限のセキュリティ要件を効果的に満たしているかどうかの判断で構成されます。最小限のセキュリティ要件が満たされていない場合、その要件を満たすセキュリティ対策がステップ 5 で選定され、承認または不承認のためにステップ 7 で管理層に提供される勧告に含められます。

contents.html: g. Step 4 is used to consider additional threats and losses not covered by the minimum requirements and to determine if they present a significant risk. Security measures are considered in Step 5 for any threats/losses that are estimated to be a significant risk. A cost benefit analysis is performed in Step 6 to determine if the security measures are cost effective. All security measures that are justified based on the cost benefit analysis are presented as recommendations in Step 7. In Steps 4 and 5, the person conducting the risk analysis may consider other threats, losses, and security measures not listed in the SRAG.
contents.html_ja: g. ステップ 4 は、最小限の要件で扱われない追加の脅威と損失を検討し、それらが重大なリスクをもたらすかどうかを判断するために使用します。重大なリスクと見積もられる脅威・損失については、ステップ 5 でセキュリティ対策を検討します。セキュリティ対策が費用対効果の高いものかどうかを判断するために、ステップ 6 で費用便益分析を実施します。費用便益分析に基づいて正当化されるすべてのセキュリティ対策は、ステップ 7 で勧告として提示されます。ステップ 4 と 5 では、リスク分析を実施する者は、SRAG に列挙されていない他の脅威、損失およびセキュリティ対策を検討してもよいです。

a. A risk analysis may be defined as an analysis of the threats to and vulnerabilities of a system, expected losses, and selection of countermeasures to reduce the losses to an acceptable level. The requirement for Federal agencies to conduct a risk analysis of an Automated Data Processing (ADP) facility has been in effect since the issuance of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-71, Transmittal Memorandum No. 1 in 1978. The Department of Justice (DOJ) issued Order DOJ 2640. 2B and its earlier canceled versions which established the requirement for a risk analysis of DOJ ADP facilities beginning in 1977. The DOJ also issued a detailed risk analysis guidance document for use by DOJ ADP facilities in 1977. A number of Federal agencies, contractors, and university professors have developed risk analysis methodologies, some of which have been automated. Due to the complexity of the risk analysis process, the methodologies generally require considerable time to become knowledgeable of its correct usage and to

b. A risk analysis does not enhance security by itself but provides cost effective security recommendations for management consideration. Therefore, there is a need to simplify the risk analysis process to the extent possible, which is the intent of the Simplified Risk Analysis Guidelines (SRAG) contained herein. The SRAG expedites the risk analysis process for the system under evaluation by initially determining if minimum security requirements applicable to the DOJ are met, which eliminates a number of threats and losses from evaluation. Although the SRAG simplifies the risk analysis process, SRAG users should be aware that significant effort by knowledgeable personnel may be required to complete a risk analysis. The SRAG is based on Automated Information System (AIS) security policies, regulations, circulars, and guidelines applicable to the DOJ as well as a review of a number of risk analysis methodologies developed by Government agencies and

c. After evaluating compliance with the minimum security requirements, additional threats and vulnerabilities not affected by the minimum security requirements are assessed to determine if further analysis is needed. The SRAG or a risk analysis methodology selected by the user can be used for this portion of the risk analysis process. Due to the increasing use of AISs other than mainframes, the SRAG also includes sections on microcomputers/Personal Computers (PCs) and application systems. The sections applicable to mainframes are also applicable to minicomputers and other remotely accessed

Various risk analysis methodologies have been developed by contractors and agencies since the issuance of the risk analysis guidelines by the National Bureau of Standards (NBS) of Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) Publication (PUB) 31, "Guidelines for ADP Physical Security and Risk Management" in 1974, and FIPS PUB 65, "Guideline for ADP Risk Assessment" in 1979. The NBS publications advocated the use of quantitative techniques assigning dollar values to system losses and estimating the annual probability of threats occurring to cause these losses. Similarly, dollar figures are assigned to the cost of security countermeasures and to the reduction in expected annual losses to determine the cost effectiveness of the security measure.

b. Although the National Institute of Standards and Technology (name of NBS since 1988) has not issued any risk analysis publications recently, they are presently considering methodologies using qualitative analysis in part or as a primary method of risk analysis. The methodologies that have been developed are primarily for the mainframe environment despite the increase in usage of PCs and networks and include the use of both quantitative and qualitative techniques. As stated previously, the SRAG does not require or preclude the use of any specific methodology and may be used to conduct a risk analysis of an AIS in many cases without additional

a. Accreditation - Accreditation is the official management authorization to operate an AIS or network in a particular security mode with a proscribed set of administrative, environmental, and technical security safeguards in a given operational environment.

b. Automated Information System (AIS) - An AIS is an assembly of computer hardware, software, and/or firmware configured to collect, create, communicate, compute, disseminate, process, store, or control data or information. An AIS will typically consist of ADP system hardware, operating system and application software, associated peripheral devices, and associated data communications equipment. An AIS includes PCs, work

d. Sensitive Application Systems - Systems that process sensitive data or require protection due to the risk and magnitude of loss or harm that could result from improper operation or deliberate manipulation of the application.

a. The SRAG approach divides systems requiring risk analyses into three categories: PCs; mainframes, minicomputers, and other remotely accessed AISs; and application systems. Each of these categories is further divided depending on whether nonsensitive, sensitive, or classified information is processed, or whether an application is nonsensitive or sensitive as defined in

b. The SRAG includes seven steps that are required to conduct the risk analysis and to document the results. The first two steps are used to provide a description of the AIS its security concerns, and the security measures

in place. In Step 3, the AIS environment is evaluated to determine if minimum security requirements are met. The minimum security requirements are listed for processing nonsensitive, sensitive, and classified information on PCs. It should be noted that the minimum security requirements for processing sensitive information also include the requirements for processing nonsensitive; processing classified information requires meeting the minimum security requirements for classified, sensitive, and nonsensitive information. The minimum security requirements for mainframes, minicomputers, and other remotely accessed AISs are presented in a similar hierarchical structure. Sensitive applications must meet the minimum requirements listed for sensitive and nonsensitive applications.

c. The remaining steps are used for the following: To determine from an analysis of threats and losses whether additional security measures need to be considered; to select security measures to comply with the minimum requirements that are not effectively met and to reduce other losses; to provide for cost effective recommendations of security measures; to present the recommendations for a decision by management whether to implement the recommendations or accept the risk; and to document the results. The seven SRAG steps are discussed briefly below, followed by Section 12, which provides instructions for using the SRAG and includes flow charts and other information to assist SRAG users. The last portion of the SRAG is the Appendix, which includes detailed information required to conduct a risk analysis, and a number of tables and work forms for use in conducting and documenting the risk analysis.

a. The purpose of Step 1 is to provide a system description of the AIS including the system hardware, software, and personnel, and a general description of the applications and data processed by the AIS. If a risk analysis of an application system is being conducted, a description of the purpose and use of the system is required. Estimates of the cost of the system components should also be

b. The detailed information required is listed in Table 1 of the Appendix and includes administrative information such as the name and location of the AIS and the names and phone numbers of AIS security personnel. The purpose of the AIS and the component functions it supports should be

c. The system configuration includes a detailed description of the physical location, system configuration diagram, connections, number of users, system and application personnel, and the application systems. A brief description of the purpose of the applications, their method of data input, and the users of the system data should also be included. Cost information required includes the cost of replacing system hardware and software, and the cost of replacing data. The cost information is useful in determining if security countermeasures to reduce the vulnerabilities and potential losses are cost effective. The information obtained during this step is important in evaluating the potential vulnerabilities of the system and the need for additional security measures. It is only through a review of all system components, the applications processed, and the flow of information that an effective analysis of the potential system vulnerabilities can be

a. In Step 2 of the risk analysis, security related information for the AIS or application is obtained and documented. The system security measures in effect are identified and documented with a brief evaluation of their effectiveness. Security measures are required even if nonsensitive information is processed to protect the equipment and integrity of the data. However, central to the determination of the need for additional security measures is the type of information processed, whether classified (National Security Information) sensitive

(Limited Official Use) or nonsensitive information, and the threats to this information. This information is important in determining which minimum security requirements are applicable. The Appendix contains a list of the factors that should be carefully considered during this step, including a list of security measures (Table and application system data sensitivity and

The security measures in place should include administrative procedures, software and hardware security controls, physical security access controls, personnel security controls, and a security awareness program as listed in Table 2 The current security control environment is important due to its impact on the evaluation of the need for

c. The person conducting the risk analysis should also obtain information on the impact of data disclosure, modification, destruction, and disruption of processing on the component's ability to meet mission objectives. The information obtained during Step 2 should be documented using Work Forms 2, 3, 4, and 5. Additional information required by this step includes the number and geographical disparity of AIS users, the frequency of use of the system, and the method of accessing the system.

a. The minimum security requirements for PCs, mainframes, minicomputers, and other remotely accessed AISs, and application systems are listed in Sections 3.1, 3.2, and 3.3 of the Appendix. The requirements of each of these sections are divided into requirements for nonsensitive, sensitive, and classified processing for Sections 3.1 and 3.2, and nonsensitive and sensitive applications for Section 3.3. The minimum security requirements are hierarchical in structure, so that requirements for processing lower sensitivity levels also are applicable to all higher sensitivity levels.

b. This step requires a review of the minimum security requirements as listed in the Appendix for the AIS or application under evaluation. The review also requires an evaluation of the effectiveness of the in-place security measures in meeting the security requirement. The person conducting the risk analysis must identify all security measures implemented to comply with the minimum security requirements, assess their effectiveness in meeting the requirement, and document the results. Any of the minimum requirements that are not met will be addressed in Step 5 where the selection of additional
8. STEP 4. ANALYSIS OF THREATS AND LOSSES

a. The purpose of Step 4 is to evaluate threats and losses to determine if consideration of additional security measures to reduce the losses is required. Additional threats and vulnerabilities and resultant losses that were not fully addressed by the minimum security requirements are considered during this step. Typical threats and losses for each sensitivity level are presented in Section 4 of the Appendix; additional threats and losses not listed in Section 4 but applicable
to the system should also be considered.

b. The likelihood of a threat and the potential loss that could be caused by the threat are considered and estimated on a qualitative basis (very low, low, moderate, high, very high) If the threat probability is . estimated as less than moderate (low, very low) and the loss is not estimated as very high, the risk is not considered significant and security measures are not considered for the threat-loss pair. If the risk is deemed significant, security measures to comply with the requirement are selected during Step 5. The applicable threats and losses, the estimate of their probability or impact, and the determination if the risk is significant
are documented to complete this step.

a. Security measures are selected during Step 5 based upon the results of tasks previously completed in Steps 3 and 4. The selection includes security measures to comply with the minimum security requirements that are not met (Step and to reduce the threats/losses where

b. Suggested security measures are listed in the Appendix but SRAG users may consider other security measures applicable to their operational environment. The security measures selected and the relevant requirements of Steps 3 and 4 should be documented. The security measures selected to comply with the minimum security requirements of Step 3 are used as recommendations in Step 7 the security measures selected to reduce expected
losses of significant threats/losses of Step 4 will go through the cost benefit analysis process of Step 6.

a. A cost benefit analysis of the security measures selected to respond to the threat/loss analysis of Step 4 is conducted during this step to consider their cost effectiveness and to provide the rationale and justification for recommending security measures to management for action. The security measures that are not considered cost effective based on the cost benefit analysis are dropped from further consideration. A cost benefit analysis is not conducted for security measures selected to meet minimum security requirements but cost information on these measures should be provided for the management decision process of Step 7. Work Form 9 can be used to provide security measure cost information or information on benefits of the required security measure.

b. The costs can be expressed in terms of dollars based on the cost of security hardware or software, personnel resources, or impact on the AIS operation. The expression of costs and benefits in annualized dollar terms where practical is recommended to provide management with a sound basis for a decision on implementation of security safeguards. Alternatively, the costs can be expressed in qualitative terms.

c. The benefits consist of reduction in the threat occurrence and/or loss impact and include any beneficial impact on mission operations due to increased protection of DOJ information against unauthorized disclosure, modification, and destruction, or disruption of information processing. The benefits should be identified and estimated in quantitative or qualitative terms. Similar to the cost estimates, expression of the benefits in quantitative terms of reduced annualized losses is recommended where practical. The alternative is to estimate the benefits in qualitative terms.

d. The person conducting the risk analysis must decide which of the security measures are justified based on the cost benefit analysis and forward these as recommendations for management consideration in Step 7. The results of the cost benefit analysis including the identification and estimate of costs and benefits for each security measure and the evaluation of its cost effectiveness should be documented using Work Form 9 of the Appendix.

a. The final step is to present the cost effective security recommendations to higher level management for a decision on whether to implement individual recommendations. A proposed schedule for implementing security measures should be provided where appropriate. Management must decide whether to provide the funding or personnel resources, or accept the operational impact that may be required for some security recommendations.

b. The alternative is for management to accept the risk to the security of DOJ information. For recommendations with significant budgetary impact, the management official may decide to delay implementing the recommendation until funding is available and should note this in the comments section of Work Form 10. The recommendations and supporting cost/benefit information should be clearly presented to the responsible management official and the decision documented using Work Form 10.
INSTRUCTIONS FOR CONDUCTING A RISK ANALYSIS USING THE SRAG.

a. The previous sections have provided a general description of the SRAG approach and the steps involved in conducting a risk analysis. This section provides instructions on how to use the detailed information in the tables, work forms, and sections of the Appendix. b. The SRAG includes sections that apply specifically to
(1) PCs, except as noted below in (2)

d. In conducting a risk analysis of a system, the person conducting the risk analysis must initially determine which category and sensitivity level is applicable. Classified information includes all National Security Information (Top Secret, Secret, or Confidential) classified under Executive Order No. 12356. Sensitive (Limited Official Use) information is defined in Order DOJ 2620.7, "Control and Protection of Limited Official Use Information," as unclassified information that must be protected against release to unauthorized individuals. The term "sensitive application systems" is defined in

e. A separate risk analysis does not have to be conducted for each individual PC. A single risk analysis can be conducted for PCs with a similar configuration and sensitivity level and located in a common physical and security environment. Also, any minor differences in individual PCs included in the risk analysis can be noted in the applicable sections and/or recommendations.
f. A flow chart of the SRAG process is contained in
Figure 1 (Page 12) . The risk analysis proceeds through consecutive steps from Step 1 through Step 7 The first

two steps involve gathering information on the system including relevant security information. The third step consists of determining if the security measures in place effectively meet the applicable minimum security requirements. A cost benefit analysis is performed in Step 6 to determine if the security measures are cost effective. All security measures that are justified based on the cost benefit analysis are presented as recommendations in Step 7. In Steps 4 and 5, the person conducting the risk analysis may consider other threats, losses, and security measures

h. The last step is used to submit all documented results of the risk analysis including the recommendations for consideration by a management official. Management either approves implementation of the recommendation or decides to accept the risk. The signatures of the person conducting the risk analysis and the management official approving/disapproving the recommendations are required

i. The portions of the SRAG applicable to each category and sensitivity level are shown in Figures 2, 3, and 4. Additional information, such as a schedule for implementing the recommendations, should be considered where applicable.

A cost benefit analysis provides a cost justification for the recommendations based on the principle that the cost of the recommended security measures is less than the benefits in increased security and reduced potential losses to the system. The security measures that can be cost justified are forwarded to upper level management along with any minimum security requirements that are not effectively met to allow management to decide whether to implement the security measure or accept

6.2. The costs include the nonrecurring costs of procuring and implementing the security devices, software, etc., and the annual costs of operating and maintaining the security safeguard. Indirect costs, such as adverse impact on operational activities or additional personnel resource requirements, are frequently the only costs associated with administrative procedures and should also be considered.

6.3. The cost should be stated in annualized quantitative terms where possible, especially if dollar costs to purchase the equipment, device, or software can be identified. The life cycle costs can be annualized by adding the nonrecurring procurement and implementation costs of the security measure to the maintenance and operational costs for its expected useful life and dividing by the number of years of useful life. As an example, if a device can be purchased for $25,000, will cost $3,000 a year to maintain, and is expected to last five years, the annual cost would be ($25,000 + $15,000) $5,000 or $8,000 per year. If the cost is the additional time that personnel must apply to implement security procedures, the cost can generally be stated in
quantitative terms of dollars per year.

6.4. If the cost is the impact on operations or other effects that cannot be easily quantified, it should be expressed in qualitative terms (major, moderate, minor) accompanied by a narrative description where feasible.
